newsitem.title: USA: At least nine killed in Texas tornado.
newsitem.headline: At least nine killed in Texas tornado.

text.p: At least nine people were killed and a dozen more were injured on Tuesday when a tornado ripped through the small town of Jarrell in central Texas, police said.

The tornado, one of several that battered the region throughout the afternoon, swirled along Interstate 35 and flattened dozens of homes as it tore through Jarrell in Williamson County, about 40 miles (60 km) north of Austin.
"I understand there is some pretty widespread devastation," Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) spokesman Mike Cox said.
He said preliminary reports indicated that all nine confirmed victims were killed inside a mobile home park and said it was possible another four people may have died.
One local radio reporter said she saw six bodies lying on the ground in the Double Creek Estate, which was hit hardest by the tornado.

Television pictures showed the twister kicking up dirt and debris along the Interstate 35 and officials said it stopped all southbound traffic for a while. Baseball-sized hail and torrential rain caused further chaos and slowed down rescue efforts.
There were also reports of people missing in a grocery store at Cedar Park, just north of Austin, where the roof collapsed when it was hit by a separate tornado.
"We transported one person (from the store) with injuries. There are reports of people trapped in there, but no further information," said Carlos Cordoba, a spokesman for the city of Austin.
A shopping mall and a housing development in the area were also struck. Officials said it was not known how many people were injured or how many buildings were damaged in those locations.
Further north, another tornado touched down on the edge of Lake Belton, destroying a city-owned marina at Morgans Point Resort.
"We have heard it was torn apart," John Durham, the coordinator of emergency management services in Bell County, said.
The DPS was urging people still at work not to drive home because of the spring storms plaguing central Texas and not to enter damaged buildings.
A tornado watch was posted until 1 a.m (0600 GMT) across central and east Texas and into Louisiana and Arkansas.
